 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day, The
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
 Oral Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)
1.
This appeal is filed by the claimant being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the MACT-XII, Ballari vide judgment dated 12.02.2021 in MVC No.843/2017.

2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
3. The claimant, as a pillion rider, along with his friend Mallikarjuna as the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA.02/BA-5604 met with an accident and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3601 HC-KAR lorry bearing registration No.AP.02/TB-3355.
As a result, he sustained bodily injuries and was shifted to the hospital.
He suffered a permanent disability.
The claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation on account of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

Accordingly,

2 prays to allow the claim petition.

sentences.text: 4. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 though served remained absent and unrepresented and they were placed exparte.

5. The respondent insurance companies, respondent Nos.3 and 4, filed a separate statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that respondent No.1-the driver was not possessing a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of the accident and there is a violation of the policy conditions.
Hence, on these grounds prays to dismiss the claim petition against the insurance company.
6. The Tribunal based on the pleadings of the parties, framed relevant issues.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3601 HC-KAR 7.
The claimant to substantiate his case, examined himself as PW.1, examined the Doctor as PW.2 and marked 12 documents as Ex.P1 to P-12.
The respondents have not entered the witness box.

However, respondent No.4 got marked one document as Ex.R-1 with consent.
8.

The Tribunal after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.3,20,400/- with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of petition till entire amount is deposited from respondent Nos.2 and 4.

Further, the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition against M/s. Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited and directed the New India Assurance Company Limited to deposit the compensation amount.

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 9. The claimant being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation, has filed this appeal.
10. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the insurance company.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3601 HC-KAR 11.

Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side and further, the notional income and the percentage of disability assessed by the Tribunal is also on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds prays to allow the appeal.
12. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Hence, on this ground prays to dismiss the appeal.

13. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
14.
The point that arises for consideration is regarding quantum of compensation.

sentences.text: It is an undisputed fact that the claimant met with an accident and sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.

The claimant produced the charge sheet marked as Ex.P-7 which discloses that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Tribunal was NC: 2026:KHC-D:3601 HC-KAR justified in recording a finding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Regarding quantum of compensation 16.
The claimant was working as an attender in the veterinary Department on temporary basis and was drawing salary of Rs.20,000/- per month.
17. To substantiate his case, the claimant has not produced any income proof.
In the absence of the income proof, notional income has to be assessed as per the schedule issued by the KSLSA.
The accident is of 2017 and the notional income for 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.
The claimant was aged about 25 years and the multiplier applicable to his age group is 25 as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation .

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimant to prove the disability has examined the Doctor as PW.2.

PW.2 has deposed that he as examined PW.1 clinically and radiologically and issued the disability certificate marked as Ex.P-9 and he has deposed that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability to an extent 2009 ACJ 1298 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3601 HC-KAR of 25% to the particular limb whereas the Tribunal has taken the disability at 8% which is on the lower side.
18. Considering the evidence of PW.2 and the medical records, this Court re-assess the disability at 10% and accordingly, this Court re-

assess the compensation under the following heads:
Sl. Heads Compensation Compensation No. awarded by the awarded by Tribunal this Court (Rs.) (Rs.) 1 Pain and suffering 45,000/- 60,000/- 2

Medical expenses 85,000/- 85,000/- 3 Food, nourishment, 25,000/- 35,000/-
 conveyance and  attendant charges etc 4 Loss of earning during 2,130/- 20,500/-
 laid up period 5

Loss of future income 1,38,240/- 2,21,400/-
 (10,250/-x12x10%x18)
6 Loss of amenities 25,000/- 40,000/-
Thus, the claimant in all entitled to total compensation of Rs.4,61,900/- as against Rs.3,20,400/- as awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,41,530/-.

21. In view of the above, the following ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The judgment and award dated 12.02.2021 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-XII,
Ballari, in MVC No.843/2017 is modified.
(iii) The appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.4,61,900/- with interest at 7% per annum from the date of petition till realisation of the amount.
Thus, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,41,530/-.
Draw award accordingly.
